title: Compact embeddings throughput & hosting exploration
next_steps: Redwood to share compact-embedding benchmark spreadsheet and cost model
Customer to provide 5k sample queries and 2k doc subset for a throughput smoke test
action_items: Nina - send benchmark sheet + pilot template - due 2027-09-09
Carlos - prepare recommended Dedicated sizing and batching configs - due 2027-09-10
Samir - share sample corpus and traffic profile - due 2027-09-10
summary: Discovery call for Sparrow Commerce evaluating whether to use Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private for an embeddings + rerank pipeline. Key concerns: throughput for high QPS, embedding dimensionality (128 vs 256 vs 1024 tradeoffs), vector DB integration and fanout, caching and tail latency, and security (SOC2, VPC/KMS). Agreed next steps include a small throughput smoke test with a sample corpus and Redwood sharing sizing and cost models.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Nina (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Nina from Redwood, joining with Carlos and Maya. How's everybody?
[00:00:07] Samir (Customer - Head of ML): Hey Nina, thanks. I'm Samir, Priya and Jeff are here too. Good to meet you.
[00:00:12] Priya (Infra): Hey. Quick note we might have brief packet loss, but should be okay.
[00:00:18] Nina: Great. The purpose today is to understand your embedding + rerank workload and decide where to run it: Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem). High level what are you trying to solve?
[00:00:27] Samir: We have a personalization search layer, ecomm catalog + user signals. We're doing a first-pass ANN search in Faiss inside our service and then a small LLM rerank to rescore top 50. Latency is a big deal — sub 120ms tail for the whole flow ideally. Throughput peak is 6-7k QPS for flash sales, baseline 800 QPS.
[00:00:45] Jeff (Product): And cost, like our CFO tried to kill my prototype so we need a path that shows unit economics.
[00:00:49] Carlos (Redwood SE): OK that's helpful. Couple clarifying q's: embedding dim now? How many vectors, update cadence, and are you open to compact embeddings (128-256 dims) vs dense 1024 for fidelity?
[00:01:00] Samir: Currently using 768 dims from an off-the-shelf model. Corpus about 60M vectors. Updates are near realtime, hundred to thousand docs per minute. We are exploring compact embeddings to save space and speed up fanout.
[00:01:14] Maya (Redwood SE): When you say fanout — you mean you take the user query, embed, then run ANN against vector DB and then LLM rerank the top-K, correct? Any hybrid recall strategies?
[00:01:22] Samir: Exactly. We sometimes do hybrid: lexical filters to slice categories then ANN. Often we do top-200 recall into a reranker. Wants to keep rerank cost reasonable.
[00:01:32] Priya: On infra side we have strict security — SSO, SAML, role-based access and we need audit logs forwarded to our Splunk. Also keys must be in our KMS if possible.
[00:01:41] Nina: Good to know. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; Dedicated also supports network isolation and can be set up with customer-managed keys — I'll confirm exact KMS integrations.
[00:01:50] Jeff: Also curious about fallback if Dedicated capacity is saturated during peak. Do you do cross-region or cheaper hosted fallback?
[00:01:57] Carlos: Yes we have routing policies. Typical pattern: prioritize Dedicated for guaranteed SLOs and fall back to Hosted compatible model variants (quantized or lower-context models) to maintain availability. That is an option we can configure.
[00:02:07] [00:02:08] Samir: Sounds promising. We care about tail latency though — even adding a rerank step can spike p99s. What batch sizing and KV cache options do you recommend?
[00:02:18] Maya: For the rerank LLM we prefer continuous batching at the runtime layer with per-customer queues; KV cache helps for sessions but less relevant for one-shot rerank. For per-request rerank, batching at the inference level (e.g., batch 8-32 depending on model and latency SLO) gives throughput wins.
[00:02:35] Samir: Could you give ballpark numbers — for a 1B param reranker quantized to int8, what QPS per GPU?
[00:02:42] Carlos: Ballpark: with int8 kernels on A100-ish hardware you might get ~100-300 qps for short context reranks, but it varies. More practically we size based on end-to-end top-K rerank cost and target latency. For embeddings throughput, compact dims give linear speedups in ANN and lower memory in the vector store, so 128 dims can cut storage and compute significantly vs 768.
[00:02:58] Priya: We host vector DB ourselves (Milvus) on k8s and prefer to keep it in our VPC. Does Redwood integrate with in-customer vector DBs or do you recommend using Redwood-hosted vector DB?
[00:03:09] Nina: Redwood supports both patterns. We can push embeddings out to your VDB, or we can host embeddings and do retrieval from Redwood if you want a managed stack. Many customers prefer hosting vector DB in their VPC for data residency and update patterns. Hybrid is possible too: Redwood runs the LLM rerank and we hit your VDB over a secure peering connection.
[00:03:22] Jeff: Latency over peering worries me — we want <120ms.
[00:03:25] Carlos: Peering plus colocating Dedicated inference near your DB region reduces network hop. Also caching top-K for frequent queries on Redwood side reduces round trips.
[00:03:33] [00:03:35] Samir: About compact embeddings — any recommended models or quantization? We tried PCA compression but maybe better to train a small distillation model?
[00:03:43] Maya: Approaches: (1) use smaller native embedding models (128-256 dims) tuned for ecomm; (2) distill 768->256 with a supervised objective; (3) product-quantization at DB level. Distillation often preserves relevance better than naive PCA. We can run an eval suite across several candidate dims and show MAP/NDCG tradeoffs.
[00:03:58] Priya: Operationally updates are a concern — if we do near realtime ingestion of 1k/min, does Redwood have streaming ingestion hooks or should we push to our DB?
[00:04:07] Nina: Redwood has streaming ingestion APIs and also connectors that push to common VDBs. For very high update rates, keeping the vector DB in your infra and using Redwood for inference is common. We'll want to look at your index refresh approach and whether warm-starting shards is needed.
[00:04:19] [00:04:20] Jeff: Can you talk about canary/rollout for model changes? We can't have rerank regressions break revenue.
[00:04:25] Carlos: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions using a prompt-driven eval set. You can route e.g. 5% to new reranker variant and monitor recall + business metrics.
[00:04:34] Samir: Great. About SLOs — can you provide latency percentiles per model and per top-K? We need p50/p90/p99 published for our procurement docs.
[00:04:43] Nina: Absolutely, we provide token-level latency breakdowns and tail latency dashboards in Redwood Console. We'll share sample perf profiles for common rerank models.
[00:04:51] [00:04:52] Priya: Security — SOC2? ISO? audit logs stored for 12 months?
[00:04:56] Nina: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we also offer enterprise compliance packages and can push logs to your SIEM. Retention windows can be configured under Dedicated/Private; Hosted has standard retention but add-ons exist.
[00:05:07] Samir: Any pitfalls with fanout to vector DB shards? We saw spikes when a single query matched across many shards.
[00:05:15] Carlos: Fanout can increase tail latency. Strategies: smarter routing to a subset of shards using partition keys, hybrid pre-filtering, or using a multi-stage rerank: an inexpensive lightweight model to narrow candidates before hitting the heavy reranker. Also caching hot queries reduces repeated fanout cost.
[00:05:29] Jeff: What about cost math — if we rerank 200 docs per query at 1k QPS average, that's huge.
[00:05:35] Maya: Exactly. Common approach: reduce recall to top-50 with a strong ANN, then rerank. Also consider cheaper reranker variants for low-signal queries. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quantization profiles to minimize token-unit cost while hitting quality targets.
[00:05:48] [00:05:50] Samir: Timeline: We want a pilot in 2 weeks and go to production in ~3 months if numbers line up. Is that feasible?
[00:05:58] Nina: Feasible. Pilot steps: baseline measurements with your sample corpus, a 24-72 hour smoke test at scaled QPS, then a sizing recommendation for Dedicated with optional Private if KMS/VPC needed.
[00:06:09] Priya: Who will need access? We'll want an SE to help configure peering and test networking.
[00:06:13] Carlos: That will be me and Maya to help. We'll also coordinate with Solutions Engineers and support on the pilot day.
[00:06:19] [00:06:20] Jeff: Any reference customers in retail?
[00:06:23] Nina: We can share anonymized references. A few retail clients have run similar high-QPS rerankers on Dedicated with VPC peering.
[00:06:30] Samir: Ok last question — if we decide to host vector DB ourselves but use Redwood Hosted inference, is there an expectation that we expose APIs publicly? We prefer private peering.
[00:06:40] Carlos: Hosted inference typically runs on Redwood-managed infra, but we can create a private peering tunnel (Private/Hybrid) with secure auth so traffic doesn't go over public internet. There are options for dedicated private connectivity.
[00:06:51] [00:06:52] Jeff: Good, that's the crux.
[00:06:55] Nina: To recap: we will 1) run a small smoke test using your sample corpus, 2) share the compact embedding evaluation plan and benchmark sheet, 3) produce initial Dedicated sizing and a fallback hosting plan, and 4) provide security docs (SOC2 and KMS integration notes). Anything to add?
[00:07:13] Samir: Sounds good. One last note on metrics: we'll want to measure business impact of rerank changes — click-through lift or conversion delta.
[00:07:20] Maya: We'll instrument that as part of the rollout and can tie rerank variants to sample business metrics.
[00:07:25] [00:07:26] Jeff: Thanks all.
[00:07:28] Nina: Thanks everyone, we'll send materials and schedule the pilot.
[00:07:33] — brief hold (network) —
[00:22:05] [noise] (middle of call) Carlos: Sorry dropped a little note — on the embedding model selection we recommend trying two compact candidates (one distilled 256 and one native 128) and evaluate with your topk/ndcg suite.
[00:32:10] [00:32:10] Priya: I pushed a quick question in chat about whether audit logs can be forwarded to Splunk Cloud — yes?
[00:32:15] Nina: Yes, we support syslog/HTTP endpoints for log export, will include details.
[00:40:50] [00:40:50] Samir: Any rough cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated for our profile? Even a ballpark per-month for 6-7k peak QPS would help.
[00:40:58] Carlos: We'll provide a modeled cost sheet but rough pattern: Hosted is pay-as-you-go with higher per-unit cost; Dedicated is committed resources with lower unit cost but requires commit; Private adds platform licensing. We'll put example numbers in the spreadsheet.
[00:41:12] [00:45:30] Nina: Final notes — action items as summarized. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot and share the benchmark doc. Thanks all.
[00:45:36] Call ended.
notes: Customer leaning toward Dedicated with VPC peering but wants to validate compact embedding fidelity and rerank economics. Security gating (KMS & audit logs) is a gating factor for Private path.
